commands.summary: Understand Terraform and OpenTofu as architecture
commands.description:
Rootform turns Terraform and OpenTofu plan or state exports into
semantic, deterministic, explainable architecture: a Form you can
explore, save, reopen, compare, and check against Policies.

Run 'rootform help <command>' for the options of one command.

A long report on an interactive terminal opens in less: Enter advances one
line, Space one page, b goes back a page, and q quits. With --no-pager, a
pipe or file, a CI run, or no less installed, the report prints in full.
ROOTFORM_PAGER names another pager, or turns paging off when empty.

Exit status:
  0  the request completed, or the answer is positive
  1  the answer is negative: a violation, an invalid object, an
     unformatted source, a failing fixture, or a name not found
  2  the command was used incorrectly
  3  the input, selection, or evidence allows no answer
  4  a file, Rootform home, network, registry, or server operation failed
commands.examples:
rootform run plan.json
  rootform run state.json --no-serve -o form.json
  rootform run before.json --diff after.json --no-serve
  rootform check plan.json -o results.sarif

commands.summary: Evaluate Policies against a Form or each side of a comparison
commands.description:
check evaluates the selected Policies against one architecture: the
Planned stage of a plan, or the Recorded stage of a state. Policies come
from the Policy Packs in rootform.lock, then the --policy-pack overlays;
--policy narrows the selection. A plan's reconstructed Recorded stage is
never evaluated.

A comparison Form has two sides. check evaluates the Before and the After
side, each at the stage selected in the saved comparison and linked
against its own semantics, with the same selection, and reports each side
apart; --side keeps one of them.

The input is a plan JSON or state JSON, compiled with the project's
Dialects, or a saved Form, loaded without compiling it again; '-' reads
standard input.

The summary goes to standard output, or the --format output when no file
is written. Progress, written files, and errors go to standard error; a
verdict is never repeated there. Every requested report is written
whatever the verdict. check never serves.

Exit status:
  0  every selected Policy passed on every requested side
  1  a selected Policy was violated on a requested side
  2  the command was used incorrectly
  3  no verdict: indeterminate, no target, nothing selected, a side that
     could not be evaluated, an input that was refused, or an invalid
     rootform.lock
  4  an input, report, or rootform.lock file could not be read or written
commands.examples:
rootform check plan.json
  rootform check state.json --policy 'security/*'
  rootform check comparison.json --side after
  rootform check form.json --stage refreshed
  rootform check plan.json -o results.json -o report.md -o results.sarif

commands.summary: Explain how one instance was interpreted
commands.description:
Show how one instance was interpreted at one stage: its Rule and Concept,
the facts it takes part in with their evidence, each closure outcome, its
dependencies, and its diagnostics. A declaration address explains every
instance of that declaration. An explanation states what the evidence
records; it never infers a cause.

The input is read as run reads it: a plan JSON or state JSON is compiled
with the project's Dialects, a saved Form is loaded as it is, and '-' reads
standard input. --stage selects the stage; the default is Planned for a
plan and Recorded for a state. A comparison Form needs --side, which
explains the stage selected for that side in the saved comparison unless
--stage names another.

The explanation goes to standard output. Progress and errors go to
standard error.

Exit status:
  0  the instance was explained
  1  no instance has this address at the selected stage
  2  the command was used incorrectly
  3  the input was refused, rootform.lock is invalid, or the stage or side
     is unavailable
  4  the input or rootform.lock could not be read

rootform explain instance google_compute_network.vpc --input plan.json
  rootform explain instance 'aws_instance.web["a"]' --input state.json

  rootform explain instance aws_vpc.main --input comparison.json --side before

commands.summary: Explain one Policy outcome recorded by check
commands.description:
Show why one Policy passed, was violated, stayed indeterminate, or had
no target, from the Policy result that rootform check wrote as JSON.
Nothing is evaluated again: each side the result records is explained
as recorded, and --side keeps one side of a comparison. Name the Policy
as <policy-pack>.policy.<name>, as <policy-pack>/<name>, or by its bare
name when that is unambiguous.

--input names the Form the result was computed from, read as run reads
it; its facts and closures then describe the evidence each evaluation
inspected. The input is used only when its Form digest equals the one
the result records.

The explanation goes to standard output. Progress and errors go to
standard error.

  1  the result records no Policy with this name
  2  the command was used incorrectly
  3  the result or input was refused, the name is ambiguous, the side is
     not recorded, the check recorded no outcome for this Policy, or the
     input is not the Form the result was computed from
  4  the result, the input, or rootform.lock could not be read

  rootform explain policy vpc-flow-logs --result results.json --side before
  rootform explain policy vpc-flow-logs --result results.json --input form.json
  rootform check plan.json --format json |
    rootform explain policy vpc-flow-logs --result -

commands.description:

non-embedded selections (Dialects and Policy Pack sources) locally.

init is explicit: it never detects providers, selects another version,
or writes rootform.lock. With --locked the existing rootform.lock is
required and valid; without it, a missing lock is an empty selection
and an existing lock is always preserved. Embedded Dialects ship
inside the release set and are never acquired. When network access is
available and not disabled by --offline, init fetches only the exact
manifest digests already pinned by rootform.lock.

Path defaults to . and is the Rootform project. Machine JSON goes to
standard output. Diagnostics and --details go to standard error.

--details lists each prepared Dialect and Policy Pack with its status
and source.

Exit status:

  2  the command was used incorrectly

     that is not installed
  4  a file, the Rootform home, or the registry could not be read or written

rootform init

  rootform init ./infra --locked --offline
  rootform init ./infra --no-input

commands.summary: Produce a Form from a plan or state JSON, or open a saved Form
commands.description:
The input is a Terraform or OpenTofu plan JSON or state JSON, detected
from its content, or a saved Form; '-' reads standard input. Export a plan
with terraform show -json plan.tfplan and a state with terraform show
-json. A configuration directory, a raw state, and a saved binary plan are
refused.

A plan Form holds its Planned, Refreshed, and reconstructed Recorded
stages, its planned changes, and the drift the plan reports; a state Form
holds its Recorded stage. --diff compares one stage of each input into a
comparison Form, which reopens alone and is never a --diff operand.

Its differences compare the two inputs; they are not drift and do not
establish what drifted between the two exports.

run serves the Form on a loopback address and opens a browser until
interrupted; --no-serve exits once the outputs are written. The summary
goes to standard output, or the --format output when no file is written.
Progress, written files, the explorer address, and errors go to standard
error. A machine format on standard output needs --no-serve. Every output
is rendered before the first is written, and none may replace an input.

run never evaluates Policies; rootform check does.
